criteria.semantics: A native <section> named by the group's label (aria-label): a region of related content, its children inside it in order.

keyboard.outcome: Passes it by: it is not a stop in the tab order.
Moves through the group's controls in order.

criteria.name: The group's label.

setting.statement: WHEN I set my text size to 200% I SEE the group's content grow with it, with no loss of information.
WHEN I zoom the page to 400% I SEE the group's content stack in one column, with no horizontal scrolling.

check.statement: The face emits a native <section> element.
The group is named by its label in aria-label.
WHEN I move into the group with a desktop screen reader (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver) I HEAR its name and the role of region.
WHEN I list the landmarks I HEAR the group by its name.

criteria.semantics: The group's children in order (in columns, with the columns hint); it draws nothing of its own. GPUI exposes no accessibility tree, so no region reaches assistive technology.

keyboard.outcome: Passes it by: it is not a stop in the tab order.
Moves through the group's controls in order.

criteria.name: The group's label.

setting.statement: WHEN I set my system text size to 200% I SEE the group's content grow with it, with no loss of information.
WHEN I magnify the window with the system zoom I SEE the group's content whole.

check.statement: A group adds no stop of its own to the window's tab order.
I SEE the group's children in the order the model gives them, the same as the tab order.
WHEN I move into the group with a screen reader (VoiceOver, Orca, Narrator) I HEAR its name.

criteria.note: GPUI 0.2.2 exposes no accessibility tree (no AccessKit): every HEAR check fails on this face today. Its SEE checks with a probe run on GPUI's test platform (gpui/src/native.rs), which no CI job runs yet (gpui/README.md, Verification); the rest are reported as not verified.
